The arXiv and Semantic Scholar search endpoints returned frequent HTTP 429 errors, so arXiv coverage is five boolean searches plus id lookups. ScienceDirect and Springer pages were blocked, so abstracts for several Thinking Skills and Creativity, Computers & Education and Education and Information Technologies papers were not read; those records rest on the title and Crossref metadata and say so in evidence. Google Scholar, ERIC, Scopus, Web of Science, CNKI, SSRN search and full-text ACM DL search were not covered, and non-English coverage is one Spanish query.

candidates.title: Borrowed or kept? How self-generation-first and direct-adoption AI workflows shape immediate unaided reasoning
candidates.authors: Liu, Guo, Gao, Chen, Zhu, Chang
candidates.task: argumentative essay with or without AI, then a parallel essay with no AI
candidates.evidence: Three-arm experiment (900 randomized, 659 analyzed): a self-generation-first AI workflow, a direct-adoption AI workflow, or no AI for a first essay, then all wrote a second essay 15-20 minutes later without AI. Blind raters scored reasoning quality, idea diversity and originality; direct-adoption users reasoned worse unaided than never-AI participants, self-generation-first users did not.

candidates.title: Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing Task
candidates.task: SAT-style essay writing over four sessions
candidates.evidence: Participants wrote essays in three sessions with an LLM, a search engine, or no tool; in session 4 LLM users wrote without tools (LLM-to-Brain) and brain-only users used the LLM (54 in sessions 1-3, 18 in session 4). Essays were scored by teachers and an AI judge and analyzed with NLP (named entities, n-grams, topic ontology showed within-group homogeneity); the outcome is essay quality and homogeneity, not a creativity score.

candidates.title: Effects of ChatGPT use on undergraduate students' creativity: a threat to creative thinking?
candidates.task: 10 weeks of ChatGPT-assisted course assignments; CREA creativity test before and after
candidates.evidence: One-group pretest-posttest design: 31 undergraduates used ChatGPT to complete assignments for 10 weeks, and creativity was measured with the CREA test before and after. 54 percent improved and 25 percent declined, with no evidence of a negative effect; there is no control group, and the abstract does not say whether AI was available at test.

candidates.title: Chat GPT como catalizador del pensamiento creativo
candidates.task: collaborative songwriting with ChatGPT by 12-13-year-olds; Torrance test before and after
candidates.evidence: Chilean students aged 12-13 wrote songs with ChatGPT, and the Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking were given as pretest and posttest; flexibility and originality rose and fluency fell slightly. The article page states neither a control group nor a sample size.

candidates.title: ChatGPT effects on cognitive skills of undergraduate students: Receiving instant responses from AI-based conversational large language models (LLMs)
candidates.task: in-class research-methods tasks with ChatGPT vs databases and search engines
candidates.evidence: 125 Ghanaian students were randomly allocated to use ChatGPT or traditional databases and search engines for in-class tasks, with critical, creative and reflective thinking measured pre and post. The creativity outcome is a Creative Thinking Scale, which may be self-report, so the study may fail the self-report exclusion.

candidates.title: The Pedagogical Impact of ChatGPT on High-school Student's Creative Writing Skills: An Exploration of Generative AI Assisted Writing Tools
candidates.venue: Journal of National Educational Testing and Assessment
candidates.task: English creative writing, grade 11, Thailand
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with 84 eleventh-graders in ChatGPT-integrated lessons or conventional teaching; creative writing was scored before and after on a rubric that includes creativity, voice and literary devices. Whether students had AI at the posttest is not stated.

candidates.title: Enhancing Adolescent Narrative Writing through AI Intervention: A Pre-Post Quasi-Experimental Study of Sudowrite in Indonesian Secondary Education
candidates.task: folklore-based narrative writing, grade 11 EFL
candidates.evidence: One-group pre-post study: 36 students wrote narratives before and after a six-week Sudowrite intervention, scored on structure, idea development, characterization, language and mechanics. There is no creativity score and no control group, and AI access at posttest is not stated.

candidates.title: Enhancing creative writing through AI-powered co-creation with cognitive and emotional outcomes
candidates.task: EFL creative writing instruction
candidates.evidence: 92 male EFL learners were placed in a high-AI-support group, a low-AI-support group (feedback from an LLM writing assistant) or a conventional-instruction control; creative writing was measured at pretest and posttest, and both AI groups beat the control. The abstract states neither the assignment method nor AI access at posttest.

candidates.title: The impact of AI-assisted composition tools on cultivating creativity among music students in Guangdong province
candidates.task: music composition
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with 120 music students who used AI-assisted composition tools or a control approach; compositions were rated pre and post on nine dimensions, including creative fluency, and the AI group scored far higher. The abstract specifies neither the type of AI tool nor AI access at posttest.

candidates.title: The analysis of generative artificial intelligence technology for innovative thinking and strategies in animation teaching
candidates.task: 12-week animation course
candidates.evidence: Twelve-week experiment with 120 animation students in GAI-supported or conventional teaching, with pre- and post-tests of learning outcomes and knowledge application. The abstract mentions creative expression but does not clearly report a creativity score; included for screening.

candidates.title: Generative AI, Performance, and Learning: A Framework for Comparing Interventions Across Assessment Regimes
candidates.task: secondary analysis of Wong and Qiu's product-improvement and invention tasks
candidates.evidence: Methods framework with a retrospective re-analysis of the Wong and Qiu 'think first, ChatGPT later' data: unrestricted ChatGPT-4 beat a learner-first strategy on expert-rated originality while AI was available, but learner-first beat unrestricted use on a later no-AI task. It adds no new participants and cites a study already in the collection.

candidates.title: Think First, ChatGPT Later: Guiding Human–AI Collaboration for Learning Gains in Independent Human Creativity
other_versions: NUS bachelor's thesis (Qiu 2025), 'Think First, ChatGPT Later: Collaborative AI Use Sustains Creativity in Problem-Solving Even After Tool Removal', https://scholarbank.nus.edu.sg/handle/10635/317435
candidates.task: creative product improvement, then product invention without AI
candidates.evidence: Already collected; listed only to add the earlier NUS thesis as an other version. 196 students worked alone, used ChatGPT freely, or used it 'think first, ChatGPT later', then all solved a second creative task without AI; the guided group had the highest independent creativity.

candidates.title: Creative scar without generative AI: Individual creativity fails to sustain while homogeneity keeps climbing
other_versions: arXiv 2401.06816 (probable earlier version: 'When ChatGPT is gone: Creativity reverts and homogeneity persists', same four authors)
candidates.task: multi-day creative idea and solution tasks with and without ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Already collected, as are both versions; listed only to flag that this journal article and arXiv 2401.06816 share the same four authors and design, so they are probably one study. The arXiv version reports 61 students: creativity reverted after ChatGPT was withdrawn, while homogeneity persisted at 7 and 30 days.

candidates.title: Emergent Learner Agency in Implicit Human-AI Collaboration: How Supportive and Contrarian AI Personas Reshape Interaction
candidates.task: individual-group-individual creative movie-plot task in online triads
candidates.evidence: 224 students were randomly assigned to 97 triads with no AI, a supportive AI teammate or a contrarian AI teammate (undisclosed) for an individual-group-individual movie-plot task. The contrarian AI raised challenge talk but did not improve creative performance; whether the final individual phase isolates post-AI creativity needs checking in the full text.

candidates.title: Student-AI collaborative creative Problem-Solving: The role of human agency
candidates.task: creative problem solving with AI; independent thinking before or after AI collaboration
candidates.evidence: From a search snippet (no API abstract): in Experiment 1 (N = 170), students thought independently before or after collaborating with AI on a creative problem; this raised agency only briefly, while deep integration of human ideas with AI output fostered creativity. Found as a citer of Kumar et al. 2025; bibliographic data from Crossref.

candidates.title: The value of generative AI in creative teams depends on when it enters collective search
candidates.task: 40-minute product-design task in three-person teams
candidates.evidence: Randomized experiment with 148 three-person teams that had AI during divergent search only, during convergent selection only, throughout, or never. AI during divergent search or throughout raised human-rated creativity and broadened semantic exploration; AI only at selection did not.

candidates.title: Sequential Human-AI Collaboration Impairs Narrative Creativity in University Students: A Randomized Controlled Trial
candidates.task: two-stage narrative story writing
candidates.evidence: RCT with 112 students comparing AI-first, AI-follow, AI-parallel and human-only collaboration on a two-stage story, with creativity rated by 10 trained raters and an AI model. The sequential models lowered narrative creativity relative to human-only writing.

candidates.title: How and for whom using generative AI affects creativity: A field experiment.
candidates.task: employee creativity at a technology consulting firm
candidates.evidence: Field experiment that randomly assigned consulting-firm employees to LLM assistance or none; supervisors and external evaluators rated creativity, with larger gains for employees high in metacognitive strategies. A 2026 theory preprint (Westover, Preprints.org) says the study also found lower later independent creativity; that claim is not in the abstract and needs a full-text check.

candidates.title: Generative AI Does Not Erase Individual Differences in Human Creativity
candidates.task: story writing and idea generation with and without GPT-4o
candidates.evidence: Two studies (N = 442): creativity measured without AI predicted the originality of later AI-assisted stories and ideas, so AI access did not erase individual differences. This is a correlational individual-differences design, not a randomized AI vs no-AI comparison.

candidates.title: Human direction drives creativity with large language models
candidates.task: brainstorming and writing with ChatGPT or Gemini
candidates.evidence: Two controlled ChatGPT experiments (N = 234 and 205), a Gemini replication (N = 157) and 6,290 naturalistic chats, with the 'creative direction' a user gives the LLM coded from transcripts. More direction predicted more original content and lower semantic similarity across users (less homogenization); the n field sums the three samples.

candidates.title: Human vs. LLM Creativity: A Comparative Analysis of Task-Dependent Asymmetry and Linguistic Mechanisms
candidates.task: propositional and creative writing
candidates.evidence: Two-stage design comparing human-only, LLM-only and LLM-assisted writing: humans showed higher originality on demanding creative tasks. Assistance from a weaker LLM produced a 'collaboration trap' in which writers anchored on the AI without quality gains.

candidates.title: Assimilating generative AI into ideation work: seeding, search and human contribution
candidates.task: idea generation by professionals
candidates.evidence: 400 professionals were tested in four configurations: human-only, unstructured human-GenAI collaboration, GenAI seeding, and a GenAI configuration built on a TC orientation; experts rated novelty, utility and feasibility. Only the TC-based configuration raised novelty. Found as a citer of Liu et al. 2024.

candidates.title: "Like Taking the Path of Least Resistance": Exploring the Impact of LLM Interaction on the Creative Process of Programming
candidates.task: programming problem solving
candidates.evidence: Within-subject study with 20 programmers comparing LLM-assisted and unassisted conditions. LLM use shortened idea generation and cut creative moments, yet solutions held about as many ideas as unassisted ones.

candidates.title: Cognitive Offloading and Deskilling in Creative Collaboration with Generative AI
candidates.venue: Journal of the Ergonomics Society of Korea 45(4), 265-275
candidates.task: creative essay writing with and without ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: 32 students wrote 64 creative essays with and without ChatGPT (paired comparison); expert writers rated assertions, opposing views, cases, concept quality, sense of agency and structure diversity. ChatGPT essays had more counterclaims, and unassisted essays showed more authorial agency.

candidates.title: Generative AI as a cognitive support tool in early-stage design ideation: A human–AI co-ideation experiment
candidates.task: early-stage design ideation from a design brief
candidates.evidence: Counterbalanced within-subjects experiment with 32 design students: a combined text-and-image AI workflow vs human-only brainstorming. AI outputs scored higher on problem framing and related criteria, human-only outputs higher on innovation, and there was no uniform originality advantage.

candidates.title: The Double-Edged Roles of Generative AI in the Creative Process: Experiments on Design Work
candidates.task: design ideation and execution by students and professional designers
candidates.evidence: Lab experiments with students and field tests with professional designers: GenAI raised creativity at the brainstorming stage for all users. At the execution stage novices still benefited, while experts spent more time without creativity gains.

candidates.title: “Who” Is the Best Creative Thinking Partner? An Experimental Investigation of Human–Human, Human–Internet, and Human–AI Co‐Creation
candidates.venue: The Journal of Creative Behavior 59(3), e1519
candidates.task: alternate uses, consequences and problem-solving tasks
candidates.evidence: Between-group experiment with 202 German participants in human-human dyads, human-internet, or one of two human-ChatGPT conditions. Human dyads scored highest on the divergent-thinking tasks, and the groups did not differ on problem solving.

candidates.title: A novel idea generation tool using a structured conversational AI (CAI) system
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39, e11
candidates.task: design ideation by novice designers
candidates.evidence: Pilot study in which 30 novice designers generated ideas with traditional methods and with an LLM-based conversational ideation interface. Experts compared fluency, novelty and variety.

candidates.title: Scaffolding Creativity: How Divergent and Convergent LLM Personas Shape Human Machine Creative Problem-Solving
candidates.authors: Rosenbaum, David, Kaufman, Ravid, Ronen, Krebs
candidates.task: ideas to make libraries attractive to young adults
candidates.evidence: 105 undergraduates were randomized to divergent and convergent LLM personas (73) or a standard ChatGPT control (32); fluency and embedding-based originality were measured. The full text (arXiv HTML) has no unassisted phase.

candidates.title: Who Thinks First? Designing Productive Friction with Engage-to-Unlock GenAI
candidates.task: writing task, then evaluation of passages
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment (N = 398) with human-only, standard chatbot, Engage-to-Unlock (AI unlocks after the user engages with the task) and time-matched unlock conditions; outcomes were effort allocation, prompting and evaluation accuracy. This is a 'think first' timing design, but the abstract reports no creativity or diversity outcome.

candidates.title: Effects of Varying LLM Access on Essay Writing Behavior
candidates.task: short essay writing
candidates.evidence: Pilot RCT: 24 students wrote an essay with no, limited (3 prompts) or unlimited LLM access. Quality was similar across groups, but unlimited-access essays were more similar to LLM output, and those students reported less creative expression.

candidates.title: Coach not crutch: Evidence that AI can improve writing skill despite reducing effort
candidates.task: cover-letter writing practice, then a no-AI writing test
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered random-assignment experiments: practice with an AI writing tool (vs practicing alone, googling examples, or human editor feedback) improved later cover letters written without AI. The outcome is writing quality, not creativity; listed because the lane covers designs on later writing skill after AI use.

candidates.title: How LLMs Distort Our Written Language
candidates.task: essay writing with varying LLM use; LLM revision of pre-2021 essays; AI-written peer reviews
candidates.evidence: In a user study, heavy LLM use made essays about 70 percent more likely to stay neutral on the topic question, and heavy users reported less creative writing. LLM revisions of pre-LLM human essays changed their meaning, and AI-written conference reviews differed in emphasis and scores.

candidates.title: Fostering children's creativity through LLM-driven storytelling with a social robot
candidates.task: children's storytelling with a social robot
candidates.evidence: 38 children told stories with a robot driven by an LLM fine-tuned for creative or non-creative behavior; children's fluency, flexibility, elaboration and originality did not differ by robot condition. A second study used autonomous LLM agents.

candidates.title: Floor Raiser or Ceiling Limiter? Differential Storytelling Outcomes with a Child-Centric GenAI System Across Individual Differences
candidates.task: children's storytelling, ages 7-12
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects experiment with 40 children comparing a GenAI storytelling system with a traditional storyboard. GenAI narrowed the story-quality gap between children by 83.5 percent, raising creativity and richness mostly for lower performers.

candidates.title: From Words to Wonder: Designing and Evaluating an AI-Empowered Creative Storytelling System for Elementary Children
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-15
candidates.task: children's story and comic creation, grades 2-6
candidates.evidence: From a search snippet (no abstract in Crossref): a mixed-methods evaluation with 40 children in grades 2-6 found that the AI storytelling system raised storytelling creativity and richness compared with a storyboard method. It appears to be the same sample as arXiv 2606.27067.

candidates.title: Reviving Reflection-in-Action: Instilling Designerly Thinking in AI-Supported Ideation through Multimodal Prompting
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Creativity and Cognition, 359-376
candidates.task: design ideation with text, sketch, or sketch-plus-tags prompts to an AI tool
candidates.evidence: Within-participants study with design students comparing input modalities for an AI creativity support tool. The sketch modality tended to raise fluency, with inconclusive differences in variety, originality and quality.

candidates.title: Inkspire: Supporting Design Exploration with Generative AI through Analogical Sketching
candidates.authors: Lin, Kang, Martelaro, Kittur, Chen, Hong
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-18
candidates.task: product design concept exploration with text-to-image AI
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects comparison of a sketch-driven T2I tool with ControlNet: the tool gave designers more inspiration and exploration of design ideas. This compares two AI configurations, and its creativity outcomes are partly self-reported.

candidates.title: InspirationGraph for Progressive Design Space Exploration
candidates.authors: Ling, Xiao, Zhou, Ma, Wei, Leung
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-23
candidates.task: early-stage product design ideation with text-to-image models
candidates.evidence: User study with 24 participants of a structured T2I exploration tool that supports divergent thinking. The retrieved abstract excerpt does not name the comparison condition; found as a citer of Kumar et al. 2025.

candidates.title: GenFODrawing: Supporting Creative Found Object Drawing With Generative AI
candidates.venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 32(2), 1978-1992
candidates.task: found-object drawing
candidates.evidence: User study with 12 participants comparing a GenAI creativity support tool (textual and visual inspiration) with a baseline in which participants used their own methods without the tool, aimed at more diverse drawings. Found as a citer of Kumar et al. 2025.

candidates.title: Generative AI: A double-edged sword for creative thinking learning — Evidence from facial expressions and fNIRS
candidates.task: creative thinking tasks with or without generative AI
candidates.evidence: From a search snippet (university news page; abstract not retrievable): 128 participants, GenAI raised creativity output scores with stage-specific effects, measured alongside fNIRS and facial expressions. Comparison condition and assignment not confirmed.

candidates.title: The effects of critical thinking intervention on reliance behaviors, problem-solving quality, and creativity during human-Generative AI collaborative learning
candidates.task: human-GenAI collaborative learning with a critical-thinking intervention
candidates.evidence: The title describes an intervention study measuring reliance, problem-solving quality and creativity during collaboration with GenAI. The abstract was not retrievable from Crossref, Semantic Scholar or ScienceDirect.

candidates.title: Symbiosis or stagnation? Investigating the impact of AI on creativity in L1 Chinese writing
candidates.task: L1 Chinese writing
candidates.evidence: The title describes an empirical study of AI's effect on creativity in first-language Chinese writing. The abstract was not retrievable (Elsevier), so design and outcome are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: From metacognitive monitoring to control: How human-AI collaboration influences emergent creativity in higher education
candidates.task: human-AI collaboration in higher education
candidates.evidence: The title describes a study of how human-AI collaboration affects students' emergent creativity through metacognition. The abstract was not retrievable (Elsevier), so design and outcome are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Enhancing human computer collaboration in design process: How AI-generated content elevates students' creativity
candidates.task: design process with AI-generated content
candidates.evidence: The title describes an empirical study of AI-generated content and students' creativity in design. The abstract was not retrievable (Elsevier), so design and outcome are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Differences in College Students' Creative Self-Efficacy, Creative Meta-cognition, and Creative Outputs by Types of Generative AI-Based Feedback
candidates.venue: Korean Society for Creativity Education journal (Crossref container title) 26(1), 1-25
candidates.task: design-thinking living lab on local community problems
candidates.evidence: 64 undergraduates received emotional or neutral feedback from generative AI. The emotional-feedback group produced higher-quality creative outputs and reported higher creative self-efficacy and metacognition.

candidates.title: EEG assessment of artificial intelligence-generated content impact on student creative performance and neurophysiological states in product design
candidates.task: three-hour walking-cane design task
candidates.evidence: 64 design students used AIGC tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion) or traditional software. Rated creative performance was higher with AIGC (d = 0.55), and EEG concentration was also higher.

candidates.title: Supporting Brainstorming with a Collaborative Platform or a Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool: An Exploratory Study
candidates.authors: Gerardini, Sarcinella, Borghesi, Pozzi, Gaggioli, Chirico
candidates.task: group brainstorming with DALL-E or a Miro whiteboard, online or offline
candidates.evidence: 16 groups of five in a 2x2 design (DALL-E vs Miro; online vs offline), with raters scoring fluency, elaboration, flexibility and originality. Online DALL-E sessions produced more idea elaboration.

candidates.title: Exploring the impact of ChatGPT on college students' mathematical creativity: A quasi-experimental study
candidates.task: mathematical creativity task
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment comparing students who used ChatGPT on a mathematical creativity task with a control group: ChatGPT raised mathematical creativity, self-efficacy and interest and lowered effort, but may hurt metacognitive accuracy. Possibly related to the collected Liu (2025) mathematical-creativity study; check for overlap.

candidates.title: The Symbiotic Ceiling in Generative-AI-Assisted Design:,Measuring Creativity, Human Agency, and Cultural Specificity in Human-AI Interaction
candidates.task: design with text-to-image tools
candidates.evidence: Mixed-method experiment with 160 novice designers in four AI-support conditions, rated on design quality, originality, cultural authenticity and visual similarity and diversity. Unstructured AI use gave more polish but lower originality and visual diversity than scaffolded use. Title copied as Crossref lists it, including the ':,' typo.

candidates.title: The Impact of Generative AI on Creativity
candidates.venue: Dissertation (Crossref record, DOI prefix 10.26686; institution not named in the record)
candidates.task: brainstorming with or without generative AI
candidates.evidence: Thesis with two experiments: GenAI use improved originality, flexibility, fluency and elaboration in brainstorming relative to a non-AI group. A second experiment scored originality and semantic distance and recorded heart rate.

candidates.title: Does Generative AI Stifle Creativity? Convergence and Homogenisation in Student Work
candidates.task: video game design projects in a computer science course
candidates.evidence: Analysis of 12 game-design projects by 36 students who used generative AI found strong thematic convergence: 50-58 percent were set in post-apocalyptic worlds and 75-83 percent had male protagonists. There is no comparison group.

candidates.title: Writing in Symbiosis: Mapping Human Creative Agency in the AI Era
candidates.task: creative writing corpus spanning the pre- and post-LLM eras
candidates.evidence: Longitudinal corpus of creative writing before and after LLMs: themes converged on AI-related topics while style differentiated. Some authors grew more similar to AI style, some less, and some stayed stable.

candidates.title: Research Novelty in Information Systems Journals After ChatGPT: Differences Across Institutional Language Contexts
candidates.task: 13,847 articles in 44 Information Systems journals, 2020-2025
candidates.evidence: After ChatGPT, abstract-level semantic novelty fell 0.176 SD more for first authors in non-English-dominant countries than for those in English-dominant ones. Individual LLM use is not observed, so this is a pre/post shift, not an adoption effect.

candidates.title: Divergent LLM Adoption and Heterogeneous Convergence Paths in Research Writing
candidates.task: over 627,000 arXiv papers
candidates.evidence: A classifier detects ChatGPT-revised style in arXiv papers, and a difference-in-differences analysis shows LLM use drives stylistic convergence in academic writing. Early adopters, non-native speakers and junior scholars shift most.

candidates.title: What Are LLMs Doing to Scientific Communication? Measuring Changes in Writing Practices and Reading Experience
candidates.task: 37,000 ACL Anthology papers (2020-2024) and LLM-improved passages
candidates.evidence: Diachronic lexical analysis of NLP papers plus 3,000 human passages and their LLM 'improvements': LLM-modified text had lower lexical diversity and distinct syntax. 20 domain experts rated reading experience in a pilot. The DOI is copied from the arXiv record.

candidates.title: Converging Naming Styles, Persistent Network Locality: GitHub in the LLM Era
candidates.task: identifier naming styles in public GitHub repositories, 2015-2025
candidates.evidence: Repositories with detected LLM-related commits use longer identifiers and more already-prevalent naming patterns, and naming-style diversity fell in recent cohorts (around 2023-2024). Marginal: the output is code-naming conventions, not creative content.

candidates.title: Voice Under Revision: Large Language Models and the Normalization of Personal Narrative
candidates.task: 300 human personal narratives rewritten by three LLMs
candidates.evidence: LLM rewrites of human personal narratives converged in stylometric space and became harder to match to their source texts, even with voice-preserving prompts. No person received AI help; the comparison is original vs LLM-rewritten text.

candidates.title: Examining and Addressing Barriers to Diversity in LLM-Generated Ideas
candidates.task: idea generation by independent human and LLM samples
candidates.evidence: Four studies compare the idea diversity of independent human samples and LLM samples, tracing lower LLM diversity to fixation and lack of knowledge partitioning. Chain-of-thought reduced fixation in LLMs but not in humans, and ordinary-persona prompts pushed LLM diversity above humans.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligences and human scientists exhibit complementary strengths in theory building
candidates.task: theory formulation and prediction on gender and race inequality
candidates.evidence: 25 LLMs vs 13 senior researchers and 60 doctoral scholars: AI theories were rated higher quality, but human theories were more diverse and gained more predictive accuracy from aggregation.

candidates.title: Divergent creativity in humans and large language models
candidates.task: Divergent Association Task and creative writing
candidates.evidence: Compares the semantic divergence of LLM outputs with a dataset of 100,000 humans on the Divergent Association Task and creative writing. Top LLMs beat the average human but not highly creative humans.

candidates.title: When ChatGPT Writes Your Research Proposal: Scientific Creativity in the Age of Generative AI
candidates.task: brief research proposal (hypothesis, experiment design, equipment, justification)
candidates.evidence: Two experts gave blinded ratings of graduate students' research proposals and ChatGPT-4 proposals for scientific creativity. ChatGPT scored higher overall and on originality.

candidates.title: The paradox of creativity in generative AI: high performance, human-like bias, and limited differential evaluation
candidates.task: egg task (fixation and original idea generation)
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT-4o's fixation and expansive (original) ideas on the egg task were compared with 47 human participants and with data from eight prior studies. Found as a citer of Kumar et al. 2025.

candidates.title: Beyond the Brush: Human Versus AI Creativity in the Realm of Generative Art
candidates.authors: Seli, Ragnhildstveit, Orwig, Bellaiche, Spooner, Barr
candidates.task: DALL-E 3 images from prompts by professional artists, novice artists or ChatGPT-4
candidates.evidence: 299 participants rated the creativity of DALL-E images made from prompts by professional artists, novices and ChatGPT-4: professional > chatbot > novice, tracking prompt semantic distance. The 299 are raters, so n is left null.

candidates.title: Using AI to Generate Visual Art: Do Individual Differences in Creativity Predict AI-Assisted Art Quality?
candidates.task: word sets for DALL-E image generation; AUT and DAT
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered online study: participants' DAT scores and the semantic diversity of their word sets predicted the rated creativity of DALL-E images made from them, with modest effects. Correlational, with no AI vs no-AI contrast; abstract taken from the PsyArXiv version.

candidates.title: Does human–AI collaboration lead to more creative art? Aesthetic evaluation of human-made and AI-generated haiku poetry
candidates.task: haiku poetry by humans, AI, and human-AI collaboration
candidates.evidence: The title describes a comparison of aesthetic ratings for human-made, AI-generated and human-AI collaborative haiku. The abstract was not retrievable (Elsevier); check that ratings cover creativity rather than only source perception.

candidates.title: Challenging human creativity: an exercise of co-creation with generative artificial intelligence
candidates.task: slogans, taglines and claims for university marketing
candidates.evidence: Compares human-generated and ChatGPT-generated marketing narratives on effectiveness and engagement; participants often preferred the human versions. Weak fit: preference-based, with only qualitative concerns about AI originality and diversity.

candidates.title: Creativity in the Age of AI: Comparing Human and Machine Performance Using Standardised Tests
candidates.venue: Springer Series on Cultural Computing (book chapter), 49-65
candidates.task: standardized creativity tests, humans vs AI
candidates.evidence: The title describes a chapter comparing human and machine performance on standardized creativity tests. The abstract was not retrieved, so check for overlap with Grassini (2025) in the collection.

candidates.title: Can I Do Better Than AI: A Comparative Analysis of a Medical Student Essay Created With and Without Generative AI
candidates.task: 3,000-word literature review
candidates.evidence: Single-case comparison of one student's literature review with ChatGPT-4o essays: the AI essay had higher Turnitin similarity (46 vs 26 percent), i.e., less originality. Very weak evidence.

candidates.title: Small-world Networks of Agents Brainstorm AI Risks to Support Ideation
candidates.task: participatory AI-risk ideation (Futures Wheel) by young chatbot users
candidates.evidence: Of 11 teams, control teams began from a risk list written by 45 AI practitioners and treatment teams from a list generated by networked LLM agents. Treatment teams identified more risks and more kinds of risk; the paper also reports model-only novelty comparisons.

candidates.title: Generative AI and Student Creativity: Cognitive Scaffolding Tool or Constraint on Originality? An Empirical Investigation in Vietnamese Higher Education
candidates.venue: International Conference on Creativity, Management, Education, Technology and Sciences Conference 2026 Proceedings, 179-190
candidates.task: student creativity and originality in Vietnamese higher education
candidates.evidence: The title describes an empirical study of whether generative AI scaffolds or constrains student originality. The abstract is not in Crossref, so design (possibly a survey) is unknown.

candidates.title: Do AI-generative tools kill or nurture creativity in EFL teaching and learning?
candidates.task: EFL teaching and learning
candidates.evidence: The title describes a study of whether generative AI tools help or harm creativity in EFL learning. The abstract was not retrievable (Springer blocked; not in Crossref or Semantic Scholar), so design and outcome are unknown.

candidates.title: Integration of AI GPTs in music education and their impact on students' perception and creativity
candidates.task: music education with GPT tools
candidates.evidence: The title describes a study of GPT integration in music education and its effect on students' perception and creativity. The abstract was not retrieved, so it is unknown whether creativity was measured on output or self-reported.

candidates.title: Empirical study on the double-edged effects of generative artificial intelligence on team creativity among university students
candidates.task: university student team creativity
candidates.evidence: The title describes an empirical study of GenAI's positive and negative effects on student team creativity. The abstract was not retrieved, so the design (possibly a survey) is unknown.

candidates.title: Is Gen AI a professor in creativity? A case study in postgraduate students
candidates.task: postgraduate students' creativity with generative AI
candidates.evidence: The title describes a case study of GenAI and postgraduate students' creativity. The abstract was not retrieved; included for recall only.

candidates.title: The impact of AI-enhanced natural language processing tools on writing proficiency: an analysis of language precision, content summarization, and creative writing facilitation
candidates.task: writing proficiency including creative writing
candidates.evidence: The title describes an analysis of AI NLP tools' effects on writing, including creative-writing facilitation. The abstract was not retrieved, and the tools may not be generative AI.

candidates.title: Critical thinking and AI-Assisted creativity in engineering education: differences between Undergraduate, Master's, and doctoral students
candidates.task: AI-assisted creativity across degree levels in engineering
candidates.evidence: The title describes a comparison of AI-assisted creativity across undergraduate, master's and doctoral engineering students. The abstract was not retrieved; it may be a survey.

candidates.title: Uncovering the effect of Gen AI-assisted learning on students' creativity: A meta-analysis from quasi-experimental evidence
candidates.task: meta-analysis of quasi-experiments on GenAI-assisted learning and creativity
candidates.evidence: A meta-analysis of quasi-experimental studies on GenAI-assisted learning and students' creativity. The abstract was not retrievable (Elsevier); its included studies may contain classroom pre/post designs relevant to after_ai.

candidates.title: Students' writing skills and creativity in the age of artificial intelligence: A systematic review of creativity across diverse AI-supported writing contexts
candidates.task: systematic review of creativity in AI-supported writing
candidates.evidence: A systematic review of creativity in AI-supported student writing contexts. The abstract was not retrievable (Elsevier).

candidates.title: Does Generative Artificial Intelligence Improve Students' Higher-Order Thinking? A Meta-Analysis Based on 29 Experiments and Quasi-Experiments
candidates.task: meta-analysis of GenAI effects on higher-order thinking incl. creativity
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of 29 experiments and quasi-experiments: GenAI had a moderate positive effect on higher-order thinking, but a limited effect on creativity. Interventions of 8-16 weeks showed the strongest effects.

candidates.title: The role of generative AI in facilitating children's creative thinking and cognitive development: a systematic scoping review
candidates.task: scoping review of GenAI and children's creative thinking
candidates.evidence: PRISMA-ScR scoping review (searches updated May 2026) covering 22 primary studies of GenAI and children's creativity, which report possible benefits for divergent thinking and narrative creativity. Its included studies are a source list for screening.

candidates.title: Can Generative AI influence creativity? A Meta-Analysis
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 AERA Annual Meeting
candidates.task: meta-analysis of generative AI and creativity
candidates.evidence: An AERA 2026 meta-analysis of generative AI's effect on creativity. Crossref has no abstract, so scope and included studies are unknown.

candidates.title: Fostering Learners' Creativity in Human-AI Collaboration:  A Review of Instructional Strategies and the Effects of Generative AI
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 AERA Annual Meeting
candidates.task: review of instructional strategies and GenAI effects on learner creativity
candidates.evidence: An AERA 2026 review of instructional strategies and GenAI effects on learner creativity. Crossref has no abstract, so it is unknown whether the review is systematic.

candidates.title: Stimulate, Don't Replace: How AI Design Shapes Human Creative Effort. The CineCoach Case and Recommendations for European Policy
candidates.task: narrative policy review on AI design and human creative effort
candidates.evidence: Narrative, non-systematic policy review of seven research areas, citing co-creation meta-analyses (individual gain, lower diversity) and evidence that answer-giving AI lowers unassisted performance. It has no new data; it may fall under the 'no data' exclusion.

candidates.title: The Creative Team Member: A Study of the Influence of AI Integration Timing on Brainstorming and Ideation
candidates.task: 12-minute team brainstorming over nine sessions
candidates.evidence: Trial registration, not yet recruiting in July 2026, with no results: teams of four undergraduates will be randomized to no AI, ChatGPT first, or ChatGPT introduced halfway, with expert CAT creativity ratings (planned enrollment 16). Listed to track a pending AI-timing study; the PI is the registry's responsible party.

candidates.title: How does generative artificial intelligence impact student creativity?
candidates.task: Alternative Uses Test (paper clip) in a college creativity course
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods classroom study: students did the AUT without technology and, per press coverage, about a month later with ChatGPT-3, scored for fluency, flexibility, elaboration and originality. Some students reported fixation on AI ideas; N not confirmed (abstract from the DOAJ record).
